mainTopic: Why a person whose land ownership is doubtful brings ביכורים without reading the פרשה, and how the doubtful fruit is handled: הקדש, redemption, תרומה and מעשר, and bringing it without the recitation.
overview: רבי שמעון בן אליקים asks רבי אלעזר why someone who owns one tree (according to רבי מאיר) or two trees (according to רבנן) brings ביכורים but does not read the פרשה. רבי אלעזר answers that even the earlier sages gave no reason. רבה explains that both opinions are unsure whether the tree-owner also owns the land. So he brings, in case he is obligated, but does not read. The גמרא then works out how to handle such doubtful fruit. He makes it הקדש, it is redeemed so the כהן can eat it, and תרומה and מעשר are separated from it. Every gift goes to a כהן, and מעשר ראשון also goes to a כהן, following רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. The גמרא says the missing recitation is not essential, and רבי זירא's rule challenges this: a step that cannot be done at all does hold things back. The גמרא answers with רבי יוסי בר חנינא's case of ביכורים that are brought without any recitation, and his proof from the פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why bring the fruit but not read the passage?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אליקים asks for the reasoning behind רבי מאיר (one tree) and רבנן (two trees), who both say the owner brings ביכורים but does not read.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי מאיר's reason for his ruling about one tree, and what is the רבנן's reason for their ruling about two trees?
steps.whatsHappening: A question is being asked about a strange-looking הלכה. If the man brings ביכורים, why doesn't he read the passage, and if he doesn't read, why does he bring?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing ביכורים and reading the פרשה normally go together, since both depend on owning the land. The ruling splits them apart: bring, but don't read. The question asks how that split makes sense under either opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: One tree (bought inside another person's field)

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּאִילָן אֶחָד,
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Meir regarding one tree,
and what is the reason of the Rabbis regarding two trees?
phrases.notes: In both cases the owner brings ביכורים but doesn't read the פרשה. If the land is his, he should read; if it isn't, why bring at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּאִילָן אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by questioning the logic of an earlier ruling about ביכורים from trees.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning that lets someone bring ביכורים without reading the פרשה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: Even the early sages gave no reason
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר replies that the earlier sages never explained this, and asks why he is being put on the spot in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Something the earlier sages gave no reason for, you ask me about in the בית המדרש just to embarrass me?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר admits he has no explanation, because none was ever passed down. He is upset that the question was asked publicly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a real answer to the question. It tells us the reason was not known, which leaves room for a later אמורא to suggest one. That is exactly what רבה does next.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעזר answering רבי שמעון בן אליקים, who asked the question.

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁהָרִאשׁוֹנִים לֹא אָמְרוּ בּוֹ טַעַם,
phrases.english: A matter for which the earlier ones did not give a reason,
you ask me in the study hall in order to embarrass me?

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר שֶׁהָרִאשׁוֹנִים לֹא אָמְרוּ בּוֹ טַעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question by saying no reason was ever given.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No known reason exists; the earlier sages did not explain it.

steps.title: רבה: Both opinions are unsure about owning the land
steps.stepSummary: רבה says there is no real difficulty. רבי מאיר is unsure whether one tree comes with land, and the רבנן are unsure about two trees, so the owner brings but does not read.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: What is the difficulty? Maybe רבי מאיר is in doubt about one tree, and the רבנן are in doubt about two trees.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה offers the missing reason: the ruling is based on a doubt. That is why it lands in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the owner might own the land, he must bring ביכורים, because he may be obligated. Since we are not sure, he does not read the פרשה, which speaks of 'the fruit of the land that You gave me.' A ספק explains why the two parts of the הלכה split.

keyTerms.meaning: He is in doubt about it

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this section is built on the idea that the fruit is only ספק ביכורים, so every problem the גמרא raises next comes from that doubt.

phrases.english: Rabba said: What is the difficulty?
Perhaps Rabbi Meir, regarding one tree,
is in doubt about it,
phrases.notes: The doubt is whether buying the tree also gave him ownership of the ground under it.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis, regarding two trees,
are in doubt about it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the original question that רבי אלעזר left unanswered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the ruling as a case of doubt
steps.terutzMaskana: Because land ownership is uncertain, he brings (in case he is obligated) but does not read (since it is not certain).

steps.title: But רבי מאיר sounds certain, not doubtful
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה: a ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר saying clearly 'because he did not acquire land,' which sounds certain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is he really in doubt? But it was taught: 'Because he did not acquire land,' these are the words of רבי מאיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה's idea of a doubt. It points to a source where רבי מאיר speaks definitely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר firmly says the owner did not get land, there is no ספק. Then רבה's explanation does not fit רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: And is he really in doubt?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא קָתָנֵי: לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא קָנָה קַרְקַע,
phrases.english: But it is taught: Because he did not acquire land,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's claim that רבי מאיר was in doubt.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that רבי מאיר is unsure about the land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's wording 'because he did not acquire land' is definite, not doubtful.

steps.title: Read it as 'perhaps he did not acquire land'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by reading the ברייתא as 'perhaps he did not acquire land.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'Perhaps he did not acquire land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps רבה's explanation by changing how the ברייתא is read, so that it expresses doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing 'because' to 'perhaps' turns a definite statement into an uncertain one. Now the ברייתא fits רבה's idea of a ספק.

phrases.english: Say: Perhaps he did not acquire land.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is changing the wording of the ברייתא, so read it as a doubt instead of a sure statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by changing the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר stated definitely that no land was acquired.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר only said 'perhaps' no land was acquired, which is a doubt.

steps.title: Problem: Bringing ordinary fruit into the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: If the fruit might not be ביכורים, he may be bringing חולין into the עזרה, which is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we should worry that maybe they are not ביכורים, and he is bringing חולין into the עזרה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the first practical problem with treating the fruit as a ספק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it is only a doubt, the fruit might really be ordinary fruit. Bringing חולין into the עזרה is not allowed, so bringing it 'just in case' looks forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: First fruits brought to the בית המקדש
The courtyard of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: But let us worry that perhaps they are not first fruits,
and he is bringing non-sacred food into the Temple courtyard!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the doubt is accepted, the גמרא asks how bringing doubtful fruit can be allowed.
steps.kashyaTarget: Bringing ספק ביכורים to the בית המקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Doubtful fruit may be חולין, and bringing חולין into the עזרה is forbidden.

steps.title: He makes the fruit הקדש
steps.stepSummary: The answer: he declares the fruit הקדש, so it is not חולין in the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where he makes them holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the first problem by having the owner make the fruit holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the fruit is הקדש, it is no longer חולין, even if it turns out not to be ביכורים. So nothing forbidden is brought into the עזרה.

phrases.english: Where he consecrates them.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fruit might be חולין in the עזרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He makes the fruit הקדש, so it is not חולין.

steps.title: But the כהן must eat the ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: If the fruit is הקדש, how can the כהן eat it, as he must do with ביכורים?
steps.simpleTranslation: But it needs to be eaten!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem caused by the last answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ביכורים are given to the כהן to eat. Fruit that is הקדש cannot be eaten, so making it הקדש blocks the כהן from eating it.

phrases.english: But he needs to eat them!
phrases.notes: 'He' is the כהן, who is supposed to eat ביכורים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the הקדש solution from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The solution of making the fruit הקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הקדש fruit cannot be eaten, but the כהן is supposed to eat ביכורים.

steps.title: The כהן redeems the fruit
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the כהן redeems the fruit, takes off the הקדש status, and then eats it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where he redeems them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the eating problem by redeeming the fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeeming removes the הקדש status. If the fruit is really ביכורים, it stays ביכורים, and either way the כהן can eat it.

phrases.english: Where he redeems them.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a step to the case
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן redeems it, and then it may be eaten.

steps.title: Problem: Skipping תרומה and מעשר
steps.stepSummary: If the fruit might not be ביכורים, treating it as ביכורים lets it escape the obligation of תרומה and מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe they are not ביכורים, and he is exempting them from תרומה and מעשר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a third problem with treating the fruit as ביכורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real ביכורים do not need תרומה and מעשר taken from them. If this fruit is actually ordinary, treating it as ביכורים means those gifts are never separated.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion given to the כהן

phrases.english: But perhaps they are not first fruits,
and he is exempting them from teruma and tithes!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא לָאו בִּכּוּרִים נִינְהוּ, וְקָא מַפְקַע לְהוּ מִתְּרוּמָה וּמַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new problem that comes from treating doubtful fruit as ביכורים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the fruit is really ordinary, תרומה and מעשר would be skipped.

steps.title: He separates תרומה and מעשר anyway
steps.stepSummary: The answer: he separates תרומה and מעשר from the fruit because of the doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where he separates them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the third problem: the owner takes off תרומה and מעשר just in case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Separating תרומה and מעשר covers the possibility that the fruit is ordinary. But this fix raises a new question about who can receive each gift, and the next step asks it.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה explains 'bring but don't read' as a doubt about land ownership. To handle ספק ביכורים safely, the owner makes the fruit הקדש, the כהן redeems it, and תרומה and מעשר are separated from it.

phrases.english: Where he separates them.
phrases.notes: He separates תרומה and מעשר from the fruit, just in case it's ordinary fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תרומה and מעשר problem and completes the defense of רבה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a step to the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Treating the fruit as ביכורים would skip תרומה and מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: He separates תרומה and מעשר because of the doubt.

steps.title: Who can receive the first tithe from doubtful fruit?
steps.stepSummary: Every gift separated from the doubtful fruit can go to a כהן, except מעשר ראשון, which belongs to a לוי. A לוי cannot eat ביכורים, so who gets it?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for תרומה גדולה, מעשר שני and מעשר עני, because a כהן (or a poor כהן) can receive each of them. But מעשר ראשון belongs to a לוי. To whom can he give it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks each gift the owner separated because of the doubt. It finds one gift that has no one who can receive it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fruit might really be ביכורים, and only a כהן may eat ביכורים. So every gift must go to someone who could eat it either way. A כהן works for תרומה גדולה and מעשר שני, and a poor כהן works for מעשר עני. But מעשר ראשון normally goes to a לוי, who may not eat ביכורים.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for this case (the opening of a question: 'this is fine, but...')
The main תרומה, given to a כהן
Poor man's tithe, given to the poor
First tithe, normally given to a לוי

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא תְּרוּמָה גְּדוֹלָה – יָהֵיב לַהּ לְכֹהֵן,
phrases.english: Granted, the great teruma: he gives it to a priest,

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי נָמֵי – יָהֵיב לֵיהּ לְכֹהֵן,
phrases.english: the second tithe too: he gives it to a priest,

phrases.aramaic: מַעְשַׂר עָנִי נָמֵי – יָהֵיב לֵיהּ לְכֹהֵן עָנִי,
phrases.english: the poor man's tithe too: he gives it to a poor priest,
but the first tithe belongs to a Levite!
To whom does he give it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 11, that he separates תרומה and מעשר because of the doubt.
steps.kashyaTarget: The solution of separating all the gifts from doubtful ביכורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מעשר ראשון has no proper receiver, because a לוי cannot eat ביכורים and normally only a לוי takes מעשר ראשון.

steps.title: He gives the first tithe to a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that he gives מעשר ראשון to a כהן, following רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. It brings a ברייתא where he holds that a כהן may also receive מעשר ראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He gives it to a כהן, following רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. A ברייתא teaches: תרומה גדולה goes to a כהן and מעשר ראשון goes to a לוי, says רבי עקיבא. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: מעשר ראשון may also go to a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a כהן takes the מעשר ראשון. It supports this with a ברייתא where רבי אלעזר בן עזריה allows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן is also from שבט לוי, and according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה he can receive מעשר ראשון. A כהן can also eat ביכורים, so giving it to him works whether the fruit is ביכורים or regular fruit. רבי עקיבא disagrees, so this answer follows only רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
The תנא who allows a כהן to take מעשר ראשון
The תנא who gives מעשר ראשון only to a לוי

phrases.english: He gives it to a priest,
in accordance with Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.
As it is taught: the great teruma goes to a priest,

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן לְלֵוִי, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.english: the first tithe goes to a Levite; these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
The first tithe may also go to a priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּיָהֵיב לֵיהּ לְכֹהֵן, כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the case within a specific תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מעשר ראשון can only go to a לוי, so it has no receiver here.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, a כהן receives it, and he may eat it either way.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole system of 'treat it both ways' works only according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who lets a כהן take מעשר ראשון.

steps.title: But real ביכורים need the recitation
steps.stepSummary: If the fruit really is ביכורים, it needs the recitation, and here the owner does not recite.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe they really are ביכורים, and ביכורים need the recitation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem. If this fruit is truly ביכורים, the owner should recite the ביכורים passage, but because of the doubt he brings it without reciting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing ביכורים usually includes saying the passage of thanks. Since the owner cannot say it here, the challenge is that perhaps the מצוה is not done properly at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The recitation of the ביכורים passage

phrases.english: But perhaps they are first fruits,
and they require recitation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new difficulty with bringing the doubtful fruit as ביכורים.
steps.kashyaTarget: Bringing doubtful ביכורים without the recitation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If they are real ביכורים, the missing recitation should leave the מצוה incomplete.

steps.title: The recitation does not hold back the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The recitation is not essential, so the ביכורים are fine without it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The recitation does not hold it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers briefly that ביכורים are valid even without the recitation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The recitation is part of the ideal מצוה, but leaving it out does not ruin the ביכורים. So bringing the fruit without reciting is acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not hold back, meaning it is not essential to the validity of the מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not מעכב' does not mean the recitation is unimportant or optional to begin with. It means that if it is missing, the מצוה still counts.

phrases.english: The recitation does not hold it back.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a requirement as not essential
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the recitation the ביכורים are not properly brought.
steps.terutzMaskana: The recitation is not essential, so the fruit is still valid.

steps.title: רבי זירא: what cannot be done at all becomes essential
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא teaches that a requirement only stops being essential if it could have been done. When it cannot be done at all, it does hold things back. Here the recitation cannot be done, so it should invalidate the ביכורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really not essential? But רבי זירא said: anything that is fit for mixing, the mixing does not hold it back. Anything that is not fit for mixing, the mixing does hold it back!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer using רבי זירא's rule about mixing flour and oil in a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a מנחה, failing to mix is fine as long as mixing was possible. If mixing was impossible, the מנחה is invalid. Here the owner cannot recite at all because of the doubt, so by רבי זירא's rule the missing recitation should invalidate the ביכורים.

keyTerms.meaning: But did he not say? (introduces a contradicting source)
Mixing the flour with oil in a מנחה
Fit, able to have something done

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי זירא's rule is a key idea across ש״ס: what matters is whether a step could be done, not only whether it was actually done.

phrases.english: And is it not? But didn't Rabbi Zeira say:
Anything that is fit for mixing,
mixing does not hold it back;
and what is not fit for mixing,
mixing does hold it back!
phrases.notes: Apply this to our case: the doubtful fruit can't have the recitation, so the recitation should now be essential.

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the recitation is not essential
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רבי זירא's rule, a step that cannot be done at all becomes essential, and here the recitation cannot be done.

steps.title: Fruit that is brought with no recitation at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by following רבי יוסי בר חנינא. In his case, ביכורים sent with an agent who died on the way are brought without any recitation, and he starts to bring a פסוק as his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: He makes them like רבי יוסי בר חנינא's case. He said: if someone picked the fruit and sent it with an agent, and the agent died on the way, it is brought but the recitation is not said. What is the reason? Because it is written: 'And you shall take, and you shall bring'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי זירא's challenge by pointing to a known case where ביכורים are brought without any recitation. The explanation of the פסוק continues past this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בר חנינא shows there are ביכורים that are fully valid even though they are not fit for recitation at all. So our doubtful fruit can be treated the same way, and רבי זירא's rule does not invalidate it. The reason comes from the פסוק that links taking and bringing.

keyTerms.meaning: He brings the ביכורים but does not recite
'And you shall take, and you shall bring', from the ביכורים פסוק

phrases.english: He makes them
phrases.notes: He means: he sets up the fruit to be like a case that has no recitation at all.

phrases.english: like Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina, who said:
If he picked them and sent them with an agent,
and the agent died on the way,
he brings them but does not recite.
What is the reason?
Because it is written: 'And you shall take, and you shall bring'.
phrases.notes: Based on דברים 26:2. The explanation of how this פסוק proves the point continues right after this.
